The client shows the login form iff allowPasswordAuth && (!login || showLoginDialog) (plus a ytAuthCluster requirement when authWay is set). |

The client stores token.csrf_token in the JS cookie ytfront_<cluster>_xsrf_token and sets global.login from token.login. A missing csrf_token or a tokenError makes the client render PRELOAD_ERROR.AUTHENTICATION and refuse the cluster page. |

The client stores csrf_token in the cookie ytfront_<cluster>_xsrf_token. |

| ✅ | GET | `/api/cluster-params/:ytAuthCluster` |  |  | Second HARD GATE. Result is cached (auto-updated-cache). A non-empty mediumList.error aborts cluster init; NODE_DOES_NOT_EXIST (code 500) on ui_config / ui_config_dev_overrides / versions is tolerated. |

The response is streamed back verbatim, so all X-YT-* response headers survive. |

## Cluster HTTP proxy endpoints (UI → proxy)

| Mock | Method | Path | Command | Ver | Description |
|------|--------|------|---------|-----|-------------|
| ✅ | GET|POST|PUT | `/api/:version/:command` |  |  | The driver command endpoint (version is v3 or v4, one handler for the whole /api/ subtree). Credential resolution order: (1) if auth/require_authentication is false -> user is 'root' or whatever X-YT-User-Name says, no credential is inspected; (2) Authorization: OAuth|Bearer <token>; (3) Cookie (YTCypressCookie / Session_id / sessionid2 / sessguard / access_token / yc_session) - and for non-GET methods an X-Csrf-Token header is REQUIRED and validated; (4) X-Ya-User-Ticket; (5) X-Ya-Service-Ticket; otherwise InvalidCredentials 'Client is missing credentials'. Bare /api returns ["v3","v4"]; /api/v4/ with an empty command dumps the command descriptors; command names must match [A-Za-z_]+. |
| ✅ | * | `/api/v3/*` | error-envelope | v3 | Error contract. Pre-flush: status 400 for EVERY error unless an earlier stage set 401/403/404/415/503; body is the JSON error; headers X-YT-Error (JSON), X-YT-Error-Content-Type, X-YT-Response-Code, X-YT-Response-Message. Post-flush (streaming): status stays 200, the partial body is kept and the same four fields are emitted as HTTP TRAILERS (advertised via 'Trailer: X-YT-Error, X-YT-Response-Code, X-YT-Response-Message' unless X-YT-Omit-Trailers). With the parameter dump_error_into_response:true the pretty JSON error is appended INTO the body between two 80-'=' delimiter lines — this is what the UI parses for read_table. |
| ✅ | * | `/api/v3/*` | format-negotiation | v3 | Output format precedence: (1) if OutputType is Null or Binary the format is forced to yson regardless of headers; (2) X-YT-Output-Format header; (3) exact-match on the Accept MIME (application/json -> json; no q= weights, no wildcards); (4) default by data type: Structured -> json, Tabular -> <format=text>yson, Null/Binary -> yson. The output_format command PARAMETER (body/query/X-YT-Parameters) overrides all of this because it is patched on top. Response Content-Type comes from FormatToMime: Json and WebJson both map to application/json. |
| ✅ | * | `/api/v3/*` | parameter-decoding | v3 | How the proxy assembles command parameters, in increasing precedence: (1) {input_format, output_format} inferred from headers; (2) the query string (i64-looking values become integers; a[b][0][] nesting up to depth 6; a top-level {$value,$attributes} map is unwrapped); (3) X-YT-Parameters verbatim, OR the concatenation of X-YT-Parameters0/1/... or X-YT-Parameters-0/-1/... which is then BASE64-DECODED; (4) the JSON POST body (only when the method is POST and the body is non-empty). The header format for (3) comes from X-YT-Header-Format (default 'json'; the UI sends '<encode_utf8=%false>json'). X-YT-Header-Format itself has NO multi-part support. |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/execute_batch` |  |  | Batch command endpoint used by the UI server for cluster-params (with robot credentials) and by the browser for most page data. Not auth-specific, but a mock must serve it for any page to render. |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/execute_batch` |  |  | Batched Cypress requests. The node server uses it for /api/cluster-params (two calls: //sys/primary_masters, then //sys/media + scheduler version + //sys/@ui_config + //sys/@ui_config_dev_overrides + master version). Parameters travel in the request BODY (useBodyForParameters). |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/execute_batch` | execute_batch | v3 | The workhorse of navigation. Sub-requests always run with an internal YSON output_format, so the batch's own output_format governs only the outer envelope. Commands with Tabular/Binary output (read_table) are REJECTED inside a batch. Each result element is {} | {output: ...} | {error: {...}}. |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/execute_batch` | execute_batch:check_permission | v3 | Fired from updateView only when the node has an `account` attribute. Two sub-requests: write on <path> and use on //sys/accounts/<account>. Result drives isWriteable / isAccountUsable; failures degrade gracefully. |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/execute_batch` | execute_batch:check_permission_by_acl | v3 | Bootstrap: is the current user in the `admins` group (isDeveloper flag)? Errors are caught and turned into false, so a mock may answer with an error element. |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/execute_batch` | execute_batch:get(@mount_config) | v3 | Fired from updateView for every node. Error code 500 (NODE_DOES_NOT_EXIST) is explicitly tolerated, so a mock may always answer with that error. |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/execute_batch` | execute_batch:get(@type,@dynamic) | v3 | Fired from updateView to decide whether to start tablet-error polling. Two get sub-requests: <path>/@type and <path>/@dynamic. Only when dynamic is true AND type is table|replication_log_table does further polling happen, so a mock returning dynamic:false ends the chain. |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/execute_batch` | execute_batch:get(navigation attributes) | v3 | The single most important navigation call: get <path>/@ with the full 70-attribute list. Everything the navigation header, the table meta panel and the schema tab render comes from here; there is NO separate get //path/@schema or @row_count call. Row count is derived from chunk_row_count (row_count is NOT requested). |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/exists` | exists | v3 | Only used on the navigation error path: ytApiV3.exists({path: '//sys/idm/lock'}) decides whether IDM is supported. Returning false is fine. |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/get` | get | v3 | Cypress read. Parameters travel in the JSON body (useBodyForParameters). Path suffixes the UI uses: /@ (all attributes), /@<attr>, &/@<attr> (link suppression), #<object-id>/@<attr>. Unrecognized parameters are kept and forwarded by the driver. v3 returns the value unwrapped. |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/get , /api/v3/list , /api/v3/exists , /api/v4/get , /api/v4/list , /api/v4/exists` |  |  | Core Cypress reads driving the Navigation page. Sent by the browser through the node-server tunnel /api/yt/:c/api/:v/:cmd. Parameters are in the JSON body (useBodyForParameters), and also duplicated as base64 X-YT-Parameters-* headers by the wrapper. |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/list` | list | v3 | Directory listing for the navigation map_node view. NB the driver default for `attributes` is an EMPTY filter (unlike get, whose default is the universal filter). With attributes non-empty each entry is a string node carrying $attributes. |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/read_table` |  |  | Heavy command; the node server resolves a host via /hosts first unless disableHeavyProxies. output_format defaults to 'json'; the UI normally asks for web_json. Parameters are in the JSON body. |
| ✅ | POST | `/api/v3/read_table` | read_table | v3 | The static-table viewer. ALWAYS /api/v3 even via yt.v4 (the command config pins version:'v3'). Heavy (the UI Node server resolves a heavy proxy via /hosts). Parameters are the JSON POST body. The row range is a YPath STRING suffix '<path>[#lower:#upper]', not a ranges object (the object form with lower_limit/upper_limit tablet_index+row_index is used only for the unmounted-unsorted dynamic-table fallback). Two calls per table open: (1) column-discovery preload with column_names:[] and range [#0:#0] for a strict schema, (2) the real page with the selected columns. requestedPageSize = pageSize + 1 (one extra row detects end-of-table). |
| ✅ | GET | `/auth/whoami` |  |  | The identity + CSRF-token endpoint. Authenticates with disableCsrfTokenCheck=true, so no X-Csrf-Token is required. This is the single gate the UI Node server uses to decide whether a session is valid; the UI reads only 'login' and 'csrf_token' from the response. |
| ✅ | GET | `/auth/whoami` |  |  | Identity + CSRF token mint. Called by the node server for /api/cluster-info/:c and (with password auth) by the auth middleware on every request. The UI stores csrf_token in cookie ytfront_<cluster>_xsrf_token and sends it back as X-Csrf-Token. Missing csrf_token => PRELOAD_ERROR.AUTHENTICATION and the app never renders. |
| ✅ | GET | `/auth/whoami` | auth-whoami | v3 | Returns the authenticated login and a CSRF token. Called by the UI Node server from /api/cluster-info. The csrf_token becomes the ytfront_<cluster>_xsrf_token cookie and is echoed as X-Csrf-Token on subsequent authenticated requests. |
| ✅ | GET | `/hosts` |  |  | Heavy-proxy discovery. The UI server calls it before forwarding any command whose javascript-wrapper descriptor has heavy:true, and uses res.data[0] as the target host. Skipped for local clusters or when disableHeavyProxies is set on the cluster config. |
| ✅ | GET | `/hosts` |  |  | Heavy-proxy discovery. The node server calls it before proxying any heavy command and uses res.data[0] as the target host. Skipped when clusterConfig.disableHeavyProxies or local mode. Real proxy: filters by role (default from coordinator/default_role_filter, itself defaulting to 'data'), drops banned/dead, sorts by a fitness function and shuffles the best half. Always 200. |
| ✅ | GET | `/hosts` | hosts | v3 | Heavy-proxy discovery. Called by the UI Node server before forwarding heavy commands (read_table) unless the cluster is local or disableHeavyProxies is set; res.data[0] becomes the target host. The browser never calls it (useHeavyProxy is false client-side). |
| ✅ | POST | `/login` |  |  | Cypress cookie login. Registered only when auth/cypress_cookie_manager is configured, and deliberately NOT wrapped in CORS. Accepts any HTTP method and branches purely on the presence of the Authorization header. Verifies sha256_hex(salt + sha256_hex(password)) against //sys/users/<user>/@hashed_password, then stores a session at //sys/cypress_cookies/<value>. |
| ✅ | GET | `/version` |  |  | Plain-text proxy version. Called without credentials by getVersions and getClusterInfo. A missing or unparseable version makes the client render PRELOAD_ERROR.CONNECTION and never reach the auth check. |
| ✅ | GET | `/version` |  |  | Proxy version string. Called by the node server from /api/cluster-info/:c and /api/clusters/versions. The UI extracts /(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)/ from the body; a missing/failed response yields PRELOAD_ERROR.CONNECTION and the app never renders. |
| ✅ | GET | `/version` | version | v3 | Plain-text cluster version. Called by the UI Node server from /api/cluster-info and /api/clusters/versions. A failure here blocks the whole UI. |
|  | GET | `/api` |  |  | API version discovery. Not used by the UI (the wrapper hardcodes v3/v4). |
|  | GET | `/api` | api-discovery | v3 | Returns the supported API versions. Not used by the UI; useful for smoke-testing a mock. |
|  | GET | `/api/v3 , /api/v4` |  |  | Command-descriptor discovery for the given driver version. Not used by the UI. |
|  | OPTIONS | `/api/v3/*` | CORS-preflight | v3 | Only relevant when ytApiUseCORS is true (browser talks to the cluster proxy directly). Handled before the API handler: if Origin is allowed, replies 200 with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials:true, Access-Control-Allow-Origin:<echoed Origin>, Access-Control-Allow-Methods:'POST, PUT, GET, OPTIONS', Access-Control-Max-Age:3600 and Access-Control-Allow-Headers:<31-entry whitelist>. Non-OPTIONS responses instead carry Access-Control-Expose-Headers with the same whitelist. Allowlist defaults: host_allow_list=["localhost"], host_suffix_allow_list=[".yandex-team.ru"], disable_cors_check=false. |
|  | POST | `/api/v3/check_permission` | check_permission | v3 | Standalone (non-batch) call from the table meta panel: {path, transaction_id, permission: 'full_read', user}. Degrades gracefully on failure. |
|  | POST | `/api/v3/execute_batch` | execute_batch:get(@annotation) | v3 | Description block on the navigation content tab: get <path>/@ with attributes [annotation, annotation_path]. |
|  | POST | `/api/v3/execute_batch` | execute_batch:get(@recursive_resource_usage) | v3 | On-demand only (the map-node 'recursive usage' content mode). Chunks of up to 200 get sub-requests, path form '<node>&/@recursive_resource_usage' with timeout 60000. |
|  | GET | `/api/v3/get_supported_features` | get_supported_features | v3 | Polled every 600 s by SupportedFeaturesUpdater. Parameters would be in X-YT-Parameters headers (GET), but the UI sends an empty object. Failure is non-fatal. |
|  | POST | `/api/v3/get_table_columnar_statistics` | get_table_columnar_statistics | v3 | NOT USED by the UI (no call site in src/ui). Documented for completeness. Heavy. Output is a bare list (ProduceOutput, so no v4 wrapping). |
|  | * | `/api/v3/read_table` | heavy-redirect | v3 | A control-role proxy redirects heavy commands with 307 Temporary Redirect to Location '<scheme>://<data-proxy>:<request-port><path>?<rawQuery>' plus Connection: close. Suppressed by the PRESENCE of X-YT-Suppress-Redirect (value ignored), by a Cookie header (treated as a browser request), or when the proxy role is not 'control'. write_table (Tabular input) can never be redirected and gets 503 instead. The UI sets useHeavyProxy:false so the browser always sends X-YT-Suppress-Redirect:1, and the UI Node server adds it too — a mock never needs to redirect. |
|  | POST | `/api/v3/read_table` | framing | v3 | Optional response chunk-framing. Enabled purely by the PRESENCE of the X-YT-Accept-Framing request header (value ignored) plus api/framing/enable (default true); signalled back with X-YT-Framing: 1. Wire format: Data frame = 0x01 + ui32 little-endian length + payload (zero-length legal); KeepAlive frame = the single byte 0x02 with no length and no payload. Framing is OUTSIDE compression: frame(compress(data)). Keep-alives start only after the driver emits response parameters, period api/framing/keep_alive_period (default 5 s). The UI/javascript-wrapper NEVER sends X-YT-Accept-Framing, so a mock can ignore this entirely. |
|  | POST | `/api/v4/discover_proxies` |  |  | Driver command (v4 only) that lists proxies from //sys/{http,rpc,grpc}_proxies or the 'balancers' attribute. Exempt from authentication and executed as root. Not used by the UI. |
|  | POST | `/api/v4/get` | get(@has_row_level_ace) | v4 | The only v4 call on the table path: get <path>/@has_row_level_ace from the table meta panel. Response is wrapped as {"value": ...}. Degrades gracefully on failure. |
|  | GET|POST | `/api/v4/get_current_user` |  |  | Driver whoami command, registered for both v3 and v4. Returns only the authenticated user name, no CSRF token. NOT used by the YTsaurus UI - the UI uses /auth/whoami instead because that is the only endpoint that mints a CSRF token. |
|  | GET | `/api/v4/issue_token` |  |  | Issues a new YT token for a user. Declared as method GET in the javascript-wrapper command table, so it never triggers the proxy's cookie-auth CSRF requirement. Used by the UI 'Manage tokens' dialog. |
|  | GET | `/api/v4/list_user_tokens` |  |  | Lists a user's token hashes, optionally with metadata. Requires the user's password_sha256, which the UI obtains through the ManageTokens password modal (it re-validates the password by POSTing /api/yt/<cluster>/login first). |
|  | GET | `/api/v4/revoke_token` |  |  | Revokes a previously issued token by its SHA-256 hash. |
|  | POST | `/api/v4/set_user_password` |  |  | Changes a user's password. Called by the UI server's change-password handler with X-Csrf-Token set from /auth/whoami. Passwords are always SHA-256 hex, never plaintext. |
|  | GET | `/cluster_connection` |  |  | Serves //sys/@cluster_connection. Not used by the UI. |
|  | GET | `/hosts/all` |  |  | Full proxy list, reachable from the browser only through the UI server's /api/yt-proxy/<cluster>/hosts-all whitelist. Used by the Components pages. |
|  | GET | `/hosts/all` |  |  | Full proxy inventory including dead and banned, all roles. Consumed by the UI System > HTTP proxies page via /api/yt-proxy/:c/hosts-all and mapped to {name, state: dead?'offline':'online', role, banned}. |
|  | GET | `/internal/discover_versions/v2` |  |  | Component versions, reachable through /api/yt-proxy/<cluster>/internal-discover_versions. |
|  | GET | `/internal/discover_versions/v2` |  |  | Component version inventory, surfaced on Components > Versions via /api/yt-proxy/:c/internal-discover_versions. |
|  | POST | `/login` |  |  | Cypress-cookie password login. Only mounted when the proxy has auth/cypress_cookie_manager configured. Reached from the UI only with ALLOW_PASSWORD_AUTH, via POST /api/yt/:c/login which converts the JSON body into an Authorization: Basic header. |
|  | GET | `/ping` |  |  | Proxy liveness. Returns 503 when the coordinator marks the proxy unavailable. Not used by the UI. |
|  | GET | `/ping` |  |  | Proxy liveness. NOT used by the UI. Real proxy returns 503 when the coordinator considers itself unavailable (no liveness, banned, or registration older than death_age), else 200; body is always empty. |
|  | GET | `/service` |  |  | Proxy start time + version. Not used by the UI. |
